note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Kew describes a persistent bunchgrass about 25–70 cm tall, with narrow mostly basal rolled leaves and a 10–25 cm often nodding panicle. Panel 2 shows a source-identified tuft, but a single photograph does not prove the crown's age.
tiles.short: Perennial tuft with rolled narrow leaves and three long lemma awns
tiles.status: VISIBLE TUFT AND AWNS; ROOTED CROWN STILL UNPROVEN

tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE INNER COLLAR
tiles.details: Use 20–40× and a 0.5 mm scale at the blade–sheath junction. The true ligule is a short inner hair fringe; longer external collar or sheath-mouth hairs are different structures. Existing gallery panels do not resolve the actual ligule.

tiles.heading: 03 · ISOLATE ONE MATURE SPIKELET
tiles.details: Published Kew measurements exclude the much longer awns. A ripe spikelet has one fertile floret and a short hairy pointed callus (~0.5 mm). Panels 0, 3 and 4 show actual reproductive structures but not a verified millimeter-calibrated same-spikelet dissection.
tiles.short: Typically 11–15 mm body with one fertile floret
tiles.status: REAL REPRODUCTIVE PHOTOS; CALIBRATED DISSECTION GAP

tiles.heading: 04 · COMPARE THE TWO GLUMES
tiles.details: Kew's broad species treatment describes a lower glume often about half the upper. Named varieties, including var. longiseta, can overlap oldfield threeawn in upper-glume length; measure BOTH glumes from one spikelet and check the lower vein, never enforce one universal cutoff.
tiles.short: Typical lower 6–8 mm; upper 11–15 mm, both one-veined

tiles.heading: 05 · FOLLOW THE LEMMA AWN FORK
tiles.details: The three-veined fertile lemma carries three long spreading awn branches, not three independent spikelets. Panels 0 and 4 show awns but do not establish the exact lemma attachment, hairy callus or ruler lengths; Kew's values vary by named variety.
tiles.short: Fertile lemma ~10–12 mm; three awn limbs ~35–45 mm typically

tiles.heading: 06 · SPLIT FROM OLDFIELD THREEAWN
tiles.details: Panel 1 is explicitly OTHER SPECIES: A. oligantha. Oldfield usually has nearly equal 18–25 mm glumes and 3–7 lower-glume veins, while purple typically has a shorter one-veined lower glume. Rooted life history and backlit glumes outweigh flower color or awn length.
tiles.short: Purple perennial with one-veined lower glume; oldfield annual
tiles.status: LOOK-ALIKE KEY PRESENT; MATCHED GLUME MACROS MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: PURPLE THREEAWN = perennial tuft with basal narrow inrolled leaves. On ONE mature spikelet the LOWER GLUME is usually markedly SHORTER than the UPPER and typically ONE-veined; Kew's example is ~6–8 versus 11–15 mm, BUT some varieties (notably var. longiseta) have a much longer upper glume (14–25 mm). Oldfield is an annual with BOTH glumes near-equal and lower with 3–7 veins. Measure both glumes on one spikelet and inspect crown before deciding; purple color and absolute upper-glume length alone are unreliable.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: Two visually checked arrows identify one spreading awn and the visible awn-fork junction on a source-identified purple-threeawn photograph. The three-awn genus character still requires confirming three branches attached to ONE lemma on a separate inspected mature spikelet.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Use 20–40× and a 0.5 mm scale at the blade–sheath junction. The true ligule is a short inner hair fringe; longer external collar or sheath-mouth hairs are different structures. Existing gallery panels do not resolve the actual ligule.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Published Kew measurements exclude the much longer awns. A ripe spikelet has one fertile floret and a short hairy pointed callus (~0.5 mm). Panels 0, 3 and 4 show actual reproductive structures but not a verified millimeter-calibrated same-spikelet dissection.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: PURPLE A. purpurea: persistently perennial root crown, lower glume notably shorter than upper, usually 1 lower vein; lengths vary by variety including var. longiseta. OLDFIELD A. oligantha: annual, mature lower AND upper glumes near-equal and rather long (often 18–25 mm) with lower 3–7 veins. Use a matched dissection of ONE intact spikelet, not color, absolute upper glume length or openness.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.caption: Purple threeawn source photographed in Idaho. A long spreading awn and a visible awn branching junction are arrowed on the actual fingertip-held florets. The exact three-awn attachment to one lemma, lower/upper glume ratio and veins are NOT resolved or measured by this image.
panels.creator: Matt Lavin

panels.label: MATURE THREEAWN · long spreading individual awns against a hand
panels.caption: A Dallas research-grade purple threeawn CC0 original shows long radiating threadlike awns and narrow attached fruiting portions above fingers. Compare an equivalent open mature oldfield threeawn image; both have three awns, so COUNTING THREE alone is not enough to identify either species. Do not label glume-vein number, lemma callus or ligule from this photo.

memory_rule: PURPLE = PERENNIAL crown + LOWER glume ~HALF upper, 1 vein. OLD FIELD = ANNUAL + glumes nearly EQUAL, 3–7 lower veins.
safety_note: Variety-aware key: Kew glume dimensions are typical, not fixed. Var. longiseta upper glumes 14–25 mm overlap absolute oldfield sizes; compare LOWER/UPPER ratio and lower glume veins with rooted crown. Need true matched local macro. 2026-10-25: a previously archived Stan Shebs 900×1235 CC BY-SA 3.0 reproductive close-up was byte/pixel verified and added to featured photos with two conservative broad-structure arrows; the separate Curtis Clark JPEG could not be decoded through the repository read and remains annotation_pending.
field_rule: Use lower/upper glume RATIO, lower vein count, and rooted perennial crown; do not identify by purplish fall awns alone.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
